justification: Data-integrity fix: a failed/timed-out ePlanning nearby-DA lookup was being served as an AUTHORITATIVE '0 nearby DAs', indistinguishable from a genuine zero. get_nearby_das swallowed its own API exception and returned [], so _safe_call wrapped it AUTHORITATIVE, and _build_neighbourhood stamped da_count=0 AUTHORITATIVE unconditionally. Now get_nearby_das propagates the failure (raise), so the brief's _safe_call yields NOT_AVAILABLE; _build_neighbourhood honours NOT_AVAILABLE (nearby_das/da_count = None + reason, never AUTHORITATIVE 0) and a genuine empty result (query ran, found none) correctly stays AUTHORITATIVE 0. Also raised the brief's shadow-layer budget 20s->30s (its Sentinel-2 step alone can take ~25s, so 20s guaranteed a timeout). The conveyancing CLI caller wraps get_nearby_das in try/except to preserve its existing []-degrade (no PDF output change).

pre_impl.existing_data: get_nearby_das returns list[dict] and caught its own exceptions returning []. _safe_call wraps a successful return into DataField(value, AUTHORITATIVE). _timed_result returns NOT_AVAILABLE only on future timeout/exception. _build_neighbourhood took a list and stamped AUTHORITATIVE.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed a failed DA API call would surface as a timeout; in fact get_nearby_das swallowed HTTP/connection errors into [], so failures looked like successful empty results.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused the existing DataField confidence model; no new mechanism. _build_neighbourhood now reads das_df.confidence to branch failed-vs-genuine-empty.
pre_impl.external_source_error: ePlanning DA API timeout/HTTP error now propagates to NOT_AVAILABLE with the reason text, shown to the user as 'couldn't check nearby DAs' rather than a misleading 0.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Backend only; the frontend already routes a not_available DataField through describeUnavailable (page.tsx:336).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a transient DA API failure rendered as a confident 'No nearby development applications' — a silent false negative that could mislead a buyer. After: a failed lookup says it couldn't be checked (with reason); a true zero still reads as zero.

functions.name: _build_neighbourhood
functions.input: das_df (the DA-lookup DataField) and an optional shadow result dict
functions.output: a Neighbourhood with nearby_das/da_count = NOT_AVAILABLE+reason when the lookup failed, or AUTHORITATIVE with the real list/count when it ran (including a genuine 0)
functions.if_none: a failed lookup yields NOT_AVAILABLE (value None) — never AUTHORITATIVE 0

functions.name: get_nearby_das
functions.input: lat, lng, normalised council_name, radius, days
functions.output: list of nearby DA dicts on success; raises RuntimeError on API failure instead of returning []
functions.if_none: a genuine empty result returns [] (no exception); a failed call raises so callers can tell the difference

values: N/A - no regulatory values; DA records are factual API output.
queries: N/A - no DB query changed; ePlanning DA API call behaviour (error propagation) only.

break_it.scenario: ePlanning DA API times out or returns HTTP 500 for a property that genuinely has nearby DAs
break_it.what_happens: previously: served as authoritative '0 nearby DAs' (false negative)
break_it.how: get_nearby_das now raises; _safe_call yields NOT_AVAILABLE; _build_neighbourhood renders 'couldn't check' with the reason. Guarded by test_failed_lookup_is_not_authoritative_zero

break_it.scenario: A property genuinely has zero DAs within the radius
break_it.what_happens: must still read as a real, authoritative 0 (not 'couldn't check')
break_it.how: da_failed is False when confidence != NOT_AVAILABLE, so da_count stays AUTHORITATIVE 0. Guarded by test_genuine_empty_stays_authoritative_zero

break_it.scenario: The conveyancing PDF report's DA section regresses because get_nearby_das now raises
break_it.repro: run generate_conveyancing_report against a council while the DA API is down
break_it.how: the CLI caller (line ~3540) wraps the call in try/except and degrades to das=[] with a warning, preserving prior behaviour

break_it.scenario: Shadow layer never populates because its 20s budget is shorter than the endpoint's ~25s Sentinel-2 step
break_it.what_happens: the shadow card always reads Unavailable even though the analysis would have succeeded with more time
break_it.how: raised the shadow budget to 30s so the S2 fetch can complete
